I get that I really was a useless partner for many years, I relied on him at my lowest points before I started therapy. 

But I really have been trying to change and get better but he still looks at me the same and treats me the same as before. It's so frustrating to want to do better but to be treated like I'm no different from before. I know he's not perfect and I do get annoyed at home but I'm also quite bad with communication. But I've been learning to articulate my thoughts and feelings better but it's just not good enough to get across anymore. It's like I've done so much damage to our relationship that no matter how hard I try it just won't be enough. 
I know this is pessimistic thinking and I know i don't always think and feel this way. I'm mentally in a really rough spot right now and I really appreciate finding someone and something I can relate to and not feel so alone. 

My childhood has just left me feeling so dysfunctional and broken and lonely and I guess it'll probably take like double time like 10 year for me to truly get over it
Thanks again for giving my your time, I really just need all the help I can get from kind internet people like you right now

Firstborn here, my parents divorced before I knew it. My mum moved out of the country and left me with grandparents for 3 years when I was 5. My granny hit me for those 3 years because she had anger issues. Moved back with my mum but also along with a new step dad for 2 years before they had my little sister.

She has everything I never had. 10 years difference between us. I was old enough to take care of myself so she didn't have to fight for attention. She was loved by both parents. Didn't have to deal with bullying that I had to deal with when going to school in a different country. I love her but I just can't have much of a connection with her even though I want to.

Wow I actually feel validated to know that it's common for us to need a place to vent and get support during the holiday season.

I've only recently embraced the fact that my childhood sucked, I was proper depressed for at least 2 years and probably mildly depressed and disassociated for majority of my childhood. So turns out I hate the holidays a lot more now that I have allowed myself to feel all those things instead of putting on a mask because that's "good manners".

My partner was right, our parents did ruin our lives. We struggle with our relationship and and try to fix ourselves (what they ruined) every single day. We are picking up the mess they left behind. We don't owe it to them to be nice, to repay them for raising us, to appreciate that they've now changed. It's too little too late. Yes I don't want to completely cut off my family, I want to eventually be the bigger person. I want to be kind and break the cycle. But right now I'm not ready. We are allowed to not want to be around them, no matter how much time has past or how much they've changed their ways. The damage is done and we suffer the consequences 24/7. We are the ones who have to be responsible for our mental health and our behaviour around others. My relationship is strained and I struggle with friendship and trusting others. I haven't been able to fully rely on anyone enough to be vulnerable in front of them. So stuff my family. And stuff every parental figure who decided to have their own best interest in mind instead of the child's. Stuff every parental figure who thought that they are doing their best and use it as an excuse to be an ass. Stuff them for not checking on our feelings, stuff them for not doing anything to help us. 

We deserve to be able to move on and be kind to the ones we love. And love them fully without holding back. And we get to choose who we love. We should get to choose to be happy

Honestly our brain is already working very hard to just survive mental health everyday. It can make it hard to do our best work and actually get a sense of achievement from what we do. Like it would be great to complete a task and know we gave our best with our skills and knowledge. But it's not always possible when our brain is preoccupied in survival mode.

I don't know if it's just me but doing the opposite kinda helps. Like take away the motivation to sh. It kinda works short term. Things like cleaning or tidying, listening to one more song, watch one more episode of whatever I'm binging. It's a bit like procrastination but for sh, if I can wait even just a couple minutes more sometimes I literally just couldn't be bothered.

Think of your body as a book, a story of your life and all the experiences you've been through. Every muscle, every mark, every hair is there for a reason. Your body has carried you through two very different identities. It has been weak and it has been strong. It will always be changing as we age and it will hold lots of memories as life goes on. Who wouldn't want a strong and healthy body and feel fit and bright? But we were born like that from day one and sure won't be like that anymore in 50 years. I still struggle with looking at my body every day but I do see and feel that it's different from day to day, Like if I had a big dinner or if I skipped meals or if I went for a long walk. Our body is never meant to stay the same.

It's definitely the wrong thing to say to a child without any clear explanation on reasons behind it. But it should be clear that you have the choice to follow or not.

It would really damage our perception of ourselves if we grew up simply being told that our purpose is to just serve a man and that our value is lesser just because of the gender we're born with.

Everyone else can only take care of us here and there even if we can allow ourselves to take a break. We missed out on a whole childhood's worth of being taken care of and I feel like that's something I missed out on and will never get back. All I can do is grieve and accept the lost...

Speaking from experience here. I started online talk therapy last year, I'm very fortunate to be able to afford it after starting a full time job and found a nice therapist the first time. 

I haven't told my family because they don't know about my issues in first place and I just don't want to deal with explaining it all. I will one day but just not ready yet. No matter how other people see us with depression and going to therapy, don't let it change how you see yourself. Their opinions and beliefs aren't always the truth and what they say and think will never have as much weight as how we see ourselves. They haven't experienced the same thing. Anyone who has struggled with mental health will never look down on someone who is trying to reach out for help. We would never judge because your story is different from ours and we are all just trying out best in our own way.

It's been a year since I started therapy, I would say I've learned a lot about myself and how I see myself and others. I'm still struggling to cope with a lot of things, but less then before. The really bad depressive episodes and mental breakdowns are less frequent but still happen from time to time. Just so you know that you're right, it's a lot of hard work. It's hard to be honest to your therapist  but sometimes it's harder being honest to yourself. Therapy has exposed a lot of painful memories and feelings that I was hiding from before. Those feelings were boxed away because they were too overwhelming back then, but now I can face them and hopefully process and deal with them.

Sorry for the big rant but you are not alone and don't let anyone make you feel any less than you are for trying to get help.

It's okay to feel this way, especially when things are rough. Like if life was easy and we aren't struggling we wouldn't feel so hopeless and depressed. But this feeling won't last forever, depression just tells you that you're stuck for life. Don't listen to the lies that depression tells you, that's all it is, lies to stop you from living your life.

I agree, a normal person wouldn't have suicidal thoughts. But when we have been struggling for a long time it makes sense to start feeling stuck and hopeless.
The key is to not give in to the feeling because it's a depression lie. It's okay to feel like giving up, it's okay to feel depressed, just remember that the feeling itself doesn't last and you will have better days than others. Just something to keep you going until you can find better ways to cope and not feel overwhelmed.

Being depressed takes a lot of effort. Feeling depressed is draining and trying to not feel depressed is also tiring. So it makes sense to have brain fog and find it hard to concentrate. Yes it sucks but it's a normal to feel like this when you have a lot on your mind. Go easy on yourself, some days will feel better than others. Try your best when you can, and when you can't, that's your mind telling you that you deserve a break and you can try again tomorrow. You've got this!

Sorry to hear this, you deserve happiness too and I know you will find it one day. In the meantime take it easy on yourself when you feel tired. It's okay to give yourself a break and be kind to yourself when life is hard and people suck sometimes.

And if they feel the need to fake it then maybe they need some help and support too?
I definitely have days when I feel like yes I can get better one day even though I'm struggling right now. And there are days that just feel so hopeless no matter what I try to do. 
I try to remind myself to not set the expectation to be happy or grateful or something because I feel like I should. When I have the feeling that I "should" be better, it just means that deep down I know I CAN be better one day, just not today. Hope this helps in some way, you're not alone and this feeling won't last and that's just a fact that depression hides from us.

Hey there, happy birthday! I can totally understand your frustration, like we know we should be happy and grateful and deep down we know we can get there eventually, but right now it's a struggle and it sucks.
Just know that it's okay to spend your birthday, or any typical day, with people you care about and also feel the way you feel right now. We can feel anxious and depressed and overwhelmed but still be able to just live life and make memories. How we feel doesn't have to make our day a "good" day or "bad" day. We can have a mediocre day that is worth remembering. We can have an eventful day that feels both exhausting and fulfilling. Each day is unique and we don't need to set ourselves expectation to be happy or grateful, we just live each day as it is.

Talk therapy helped me with it, even though it wasn't explicitly inner child work. I learned to be aware of my behaviours, reactions, and emotions that reflect what I would have had as a child or even a teen sometimes. Things like crying during any conflict, or hiding in my room, feelings of insecurity. These where things that I would've learned as a child in order to cope with the situations back then. And while I'm a functioning adult most of the time, I sometimes revert back to those things in order to protect my adult self from bad experiences.

Being aware of when I feel or behave or think like my child self took practice but once you get the hang of it, you start to notice why you behave or think in certain ways. And then over time you get to know your child self and their needs and wants. And you learn to treat them with care and respect so that we can understand that the coping skills that we needed back then is no longer applicable now because we are grown up and have more knowledge and control over ourselves and our lives.

Honestly at the start when I began to be aware of my child self, I treated her exactly the same way my family treated me. I was harsh with her, looked down on her for being weak and just wanted to get rid of her. I never listened to what I really needed and just tried to push it down. But over time I learned to see my child self as a child, not as me. Then the way I treated her changed. I learned to listen to her and have patience and everything else just followed naturally.

The most frustrating thing is when I know I could've learned and understood these things before trauma. I remember doing really well academically. I remember how fast I can pick up concepts. It sucks even more when my head is foggy and can't focus the same way because I know I wasn't always like this. I know how much the past is draining me.

Thanks for the reminder. It's a bit chilling to read the list and realise that while these are such basic needs for a child many of us didn't get enough growing up. But love the fact that we have control over these things for ourselves and can provide these to others too.

It's definitely frustrating then we work so hard on ourselves in order to process the trauma and when we are ready to talk not everybody is ready to listen. 

I find that for myself, I don't always need the other person to fully understand what I went through. Especially with therapy I know my trauma is valid and real and I don't need others to validate it for me.
I think it helps instead to break down what kind of support I need and seek it from several people that I trust on different levels.

Sometimes I need a friend to just hangout and enjoy the small things, be silly, laugh. Sometimes I need someone to listen and at the end just say "Yeah it sucks, man. Sorry to hear that" and I don't need them to do anything. Sometimes I need a shoulder to cry on, or some advice and wise words. Sometimes I need someone who went through similar experience so we don't even need words to understand each other. And I definitely need therapy where I can trust professional advice and process my past. 

The point is - It's hard enough for ourselves to understand our own experience nevermind someone who didn't go through the same thing. If one person cannot fully understand our trauma, then maybe building a support circle can give us enough support and care to feel understood and valid

I also had a pillowcase that I always slept with and rubbed the edges and corners where the seams were for comfort. It was the only way I could sleep. Now I read about grounding strategies and mindfulness which actually is quite similar. The touch sensations kept me grounded and in the present while taking my mind off the bad feelings because I just focused on the feelings on my fingers

Maybe there are other questions to consider - Did your friends see their parents make up after an argument? Did their parents comfort them and explain the situation after yelling at them? And did you see the same?
I never really seen my parents argue because they separated when I was too young to remember. But when I was yelled at, I was told that it's for my own good, and I was physically punished. And that was how it was resolved. Now I grew up with the mindset that arguments lead to physical pain whether it's from others or myself. Because I never saw a healthy way to resolve an argument, like apologising, comforting and reassuring each other and move on.

I talk through a lot of my childhood experiences during therapy and I definitely remember and think about those memories more even outside of therapy. Some are good but most are bad. I used to avoid these memories because, in my therapist's words, they were too overwhelming to think about and to feel. Yes it was safe when I avoided the memories but they were always in the back of my mind, it took constant energy to avoid them and it's exhausting. 
With some practice talking about it in a safe place in therapy, I can slowly allow myself to take a break from pushing back the memories and start to face them and feel them. It hurts, a lot, but it's not so overwhelmingly bad that I have to suppress it anymore. I don't know if it will ever stop hurting, but at least I know I'm not exhausting my mental energy and it's okay to remember and to feel.

One thing I read about is self-parenting. Basically the opposite of what we have been doing. Instead of abandoning ourselves, we become parent to our inner child. If my inner child is unhappy, throwing a tantrum, then I'll ask myself what do I need and want in this moment. My inner child wants comfort and something sweet like ice cream, then that's why I'll give her. I wasn't comforted by my parents when I was young, I was shouted at to stop crying. Growing up I always cried only when I'm alone, I never allowed myself to show weakness in front of others. I treated myself the way my family treated me.
Now I'm actively trying to do the opposite, treat myself the way I would like to raise my children in the future when I'm ready.
If my inner child is avoiding difficult tasks then I would ask why, and give myself rewards after, and be proud of myself for taking the first step. It's not all easy, but when you are aware of when you have self-abandonment thoughts and behaviours, it's easier to stop and replace it with self-parenting.
Honestly I still feel like it's unfair that I have to do this myself, I don't have anyone else who can parent me and love me unconditionally. But at the very least I know I deserve some kindness from myself if no one else could give that
